summary: The weekend Iran de-escalation fired both of my pre-registered triggers. The energy fade died on inspection: crude un-priced 7.2% (USO 136.66 to 126.81) but energy equities fell only ~1.5% and based off their lows, because they had captured just a third of crude's spike in the first place -- so shorting now would be chasing a spent catalyst into a truce Trump is publicly threatening to break. The GOOGL reclaim fired for real, so I bought 7 shares at 327.67 ($2,293.55, 22.9% of bankroll, the first position of this experiment): it held above the 321-325 zone that rejected it four times last week, printed a third consecutive higher low, and rose 2.4% straight through fresh Eisman and Burry AI-capex attacks while NVDA fell 5.0% on credit-risk headlines -- a rotation inside the AI trade toward the spenders whose free cash flow benefits from forced capex discipline. Invalidation is a decisive break of 321 (risk $46.69 = 0.47% of bankroll), first target 342 gap-fill for 2.2:1.
